title: Introduction to Bioinformatics — Pre/Post Test
notes: No participant code; pairing uses the signed-in dashboard account.
Only knowledge-check MCQs are auto-scored (I don't know yet = 0).
Background, confidence, and reflection items are stored but not scored.
Suggested time: 10 minutes per test. Do not show the answer key until both tests are complete.

pre_test.question: Which best describes your current role?
Before this training, how much experience had you had with the Linux terminal or command line?
options: None - I am new to the command line
I have seen someone use it or heard about it
I have read about it or attended a lecture
I have completed guided command-line exercises
I regularly use the command line independently

pre_test.question: How often did you use a terminal or command-line interface before this training?
options: One to three times a month
One or more times a week

pre_test.question: Which command-line skills have you used before? Select all that apply.
options: Creating, copying, moving, or deleting files and directories
Searching or processing text with commands such as `grep`, `sort`, or `wc`
Combining commands with pipes or redirection

pre_test.question: Which skill would you most like to develop during this training? Select one.
options: Understanding the terminal and command structure
Creating and managing files and directories
Viewing, editing, and searching text files
Combining commands with pipes and redirection

pre_test.question: I can explain what a terminal is and identify the command, options, and arguments in a command.
pre_test.sectionIntro: Rate your confidence before training using this scale: 1 = Not at all confident; 2 = Slightly confident; 3 = Moderately confident; 4 = Very confident; 5 = Extremely confident

pre_test.question: I can navigate the Linux file system using paths and basic commands.
I can create, copy, move, rename, and safely delete files and directories.
I can view, edit, search, sort, and count information in text files.
I can use pipes, redirection, wildcards, and file permissions in command-line tasks.
Why is the command line especially useful for data analysis and bioinformatics?
options: It only works with small files that can be opened manually
It makes every task graphical and mouse-driven
It supports fast, reproducible, and scalable workflows
It automatically corrects every command before running it

The file that will be searched

options: Saves output directly to a new file

Runs the command with administrator permission

options: `>` overwrites the destination file, while `>>` appends to it

`>` copies a file, while `>>` moves it
There is no difference between them
